chapter: Leading the band after Chick Webb, 1939-40
title: Duke Ellington's "Jump for Joy" in Los Angeles
summary: McRae praises Duke's show, took Ella to see it, and recalls Ben Webster stumbling into the pit.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Now we came back to play the theater in California.
Now is when Duke is out on the coast. Then is when he was writing 'Jump For Joy.' This is the show that never came to New York.
This was a great show. Even greater than Sophisticated Ladies, Sophisticated Ladies didn't show come nowhere near this (inaudible).
I think Jack Robbins -- Jerome Robbins bought that book by Duke. It's never been produced.

I used to talk to Duke just before -- all the time. I used to hang out with Duke and I say, 'Why don't you produce Jump For Joy,' you know, 'over here,' you know. And he'd always, 'I'll get around to it.' (inaudible). But that was a great show.
I took Ella to see that show.
And like I tell you, when we was sitting

down in the front row, and Ben Webster was the Beck's pet bad boy, here comes Ben out there, stumbling, knocking over -- he's was the noisiest one getting out in the pit. The theater's quiet.
Up there at that time was Ethel Waters. She was there. She was in Cabin In The Sky.
I took Ella to see Ethel Waters, Cabin In The Sky. She never had been to see no show.
I used to take her to see all these shows. I say, "I'm going to take you to see Ethel Waters. You'll see Cabin In The Sky."
